key_insight: The paper introduces a backward-mapping, genome-guided workflow that translates device-level goals into interpretable chemical descriptors to discover phase-stable, lead-free double perovskites.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, explainable screening of Pb-free perovskites for optoelectronic devices by coupling stability, band-gap targeting, and DFT validation.
method: Start with 13,088 charge-balanced A2BB'X6 compositions and apply halide-aware geometric formability filtering.
Encode candidates with six families of chemical-genome descriptors and train evolutionary-optimized ML surrogates for stability and band gap.
Use SHAP interpretation plus DFT phenotype closure to validate seven final candidates and derive design rules.
evidence_signal: The workflow narrows 13,088 compositions to seven DFT-validated candidates and verifies them with structural assignability, electronic, optical, dielectric, transport, and XRD analyses.
watch_item: Because the models are trained on surrogate labels and validated on a small set of finalists, transferability to broader chemistries and experimental synthesis still needs careful confirmation.
paper_title: Backward Mapping from Device Targets to Chemical Genomes for Interpretable Discovery of Phase-Stable Lead-Free Double Perovskites with DFT-Validated Design Rules
